answer: A reputation bond stops cheap fake identities: each agent must lock a small refundable stake before it can trade, and the stake is slashed if peers prove fraud. Like a river that only an oasis can sustain in a desert, honest history accumulates slowly through verified work, while a whisper of new accounts cannot buy trust instantly. An attacker must fund, age, and risk a separate stake for every fake identity, so mass forgery costs far more than it can earn.
